exclusions.A: He pressed the low C once and listened to it fade.
exclusions.C: The piano stood where it always had, at the far end from the stove.
exclusions.D: It struck Abel, running his thumb along it, that Rusk had known from the start how this would end.
exclusions.E: But the split now ran the width of the board, and a tuning held there for a week at most.

WV10-P01.4.note: 'It struck Abel ... that Rusk had known' is the idiom for a realization occurring to him, i.e. it dawned on him; 'concluded' implies deliberate reasoning the sentence does not describe, and pressing/igniting/removing are literal senses with no fit.

exclusions.A: Abel kept his hand on the lid.
exclusions.C: That's gone now, and tuning won't fetch it back.'
exclusions.E: He pressed the low C once and listened to it fade.

WV10-P01.5.note: He recalls how the bass 'rang like a bell' twenty years ago and accepts it is gone, a fond, sad look back; he assures Nell it will be ready, so not worried, and nothing signals anger, thanks or amusement.

exclusions.A: The dispute ran through eleven meetings and two winters, until a councillor raised the matter of the common's drains and the yard won by one vote.
exclusions.B: Nora wanted it on the common; the council wanted the station yard.
exclusions.D: Where the carousel would stand was another matter.
exclusions.E: By then the raffle, its tickets printed with a photograph taken in 1923 of the carousel in full swing, had sold out in a week and paid for the restoration.

WV10-P02.4.note: A councillor 'raised the matter' of the drains in a meeting dispute, i.e. brought it up or mentioned it; the money was raised by the raffle, not by the councillor, and nothing is lifted, increased or bred.

exclusions.A: He hitched up the trailer that afternoon.
exclusions.C: When she asked for the grey, he told her she could have it if she could catch it, and led her to a stall where the wooden horse stood between his two real ones, wearing a halter, a bucket of oats at its feet.
exclusions.D: Hal and Nora had sung side by side in the chapel choir for twenty years.
exclusions.E: That left the grey, which Hal Brigg's father had bought at the auction.

WV10-P02.5.note: Telling her she can have the wooden horse 'if she could catch it' and staging it in a stall with a halter and oats is a joke; he then hands it over the same afternoon, so no anger, worry, or looking back is shown.

exclusions.B: In May a boardwalk opened, with lamps that switch off at ten, hours before the beetles stir, and visitors began to stray from it onto the dune.
exclusions.C: Last July, her student Joel Arkin's first on the spit, the count fell from its usual eight hundred to two hundred and sixty.
exclusions.D: This July the count was seven hundred and eighty; last year's figure, she now writes, measured the traps rather than the beetles.
exclusions.E: A March storm tore away the dune's seaward face and much of the old crest with it.

WV10-P03.4.note: A sand fence that 'ran the whole length of the dune foot' stretched or extended along it; it is a physical structure, not a machine operated, a sum, a publication, or a flow.

exclusions.A: Vell moved the traps up onto the new crest.
exclusions.C: Vell said he would be the one to tell them, and slid the season report across the desk.
exclusions.D: She had crossed out her own name on its first page and written his above it.
exclusions.E: This July the count was seven hundred and eighty; last year's figure, she now writes, measured the traps rather than the beetles.

WV10-P03.5.note: Giving Arkin the job of telling the park and putting his name above hers on the report credits his discovery, showing admiration; she acts calmly and earnestly, with no sign of worry, irritation, teasing or longing.
